claims.statement: Rules 200, 210, and 220 are internal pre-bind and renewal underwriting controls for property risk selection, referral, holds, conditions, and documentation; they do not alter coverage, which remains governed by the applicable carrier-issued form, declarations, and attached endorsements.

Rule 200 requires construction information to be complete and classified by predominant exterior-wall construction, requires reliable protection-class verification, and refers unsupported construction, access, fire-water, and response information before final underwriting action.

Rule 200 requires a wind mitigation inspection before final underwriting action when Coverage A exceeds $750,000 and requires review of material roof, attachment, and opening-protection information when wind exposure is material.

Rule 210 requires roof inspection findings before binding at roof age 15 years or greater and holds binding authority until acceptable condition is supported; it requires decline at roof age 25 years or greater without discretionary override.

Rule 210 requires reliable evidence for roof age and replacement scope and refers deteriorated, damaged, leaking, inadequately repaired, materially worn, inaccessible, or otherwise unverified roof conditions; required corrections must be completed and documented before binding when necessary.

Rule 220 requires identification of water sources and prior water damage and requires referral of active leakage, moisture staining, mold evidence, wet materials, or unresolved water entry; binding may not proceed while the Rule 220.C condition remains unresolved.

Rule 220 routes plumbing, appliance, water-heater, freeze, vacancy, drainage, sump, sewer, septic, check-valve, and recurring-water-loss conditions to evidence review, corrective action, or referral when the source or repair status is unresolved.

Rule 220 requires referral for a requested water-backup limit above $25,000 and requires the backup deductible to be available for and approved by underwriting, with authorized approval before alteration; when attached, the water-backup endorsement controls the contractual limit and deductible. HO 04 90 (2027-01) states a $10,000 limit of liability and a $1,000 deductible for each covered water-backup loss.

Rule 210's roof-age thresholds constrain underwriting eligibility rather than claim settlement; when attached and applicable, HO 23 74 2025-05 separately applies actual-cash-value treatment to covered roof surfacing at Roof Age 12 years or greater using reliable age evidence.

When Rule 220 water-exposure information is insufficient, the Manual prohibits binding until the missing information is obtained or authorized direction is recorded and requires a clear note of the condition, evidence, referral activity, and final action.

Rule 100 makes inspection currency and referral records part of the general underwriting lifecycle by treating an inspection report as current for 12 months after receipt, requiring resolution of material inspection concerns before final action, and requiring authorized approval conditions to be recorded.

Rules 310 and 320 overlay the detailed property controls: Rule 310 mandates referral with a binding or processing hold for open or disputed claims, vacancy or unoccupancy, ongoing renovation, structural or roof damage, recurring water intrusion, unresolved plumbing leakage, sewer or drain backup, and suspected mold, fungi, or rot; Rule 320 requires decline when a known materially loss-increasing condition cannot be corrected before binding, including unresolved roof damage or leakage, active water intrusion, unrepaired plumbing failure, and unresolved active mold, fungal growth, rot, or moisture damage.

Rule 240.S requires review of prior claims involving mold, fungi, bacteria, rot, or moisture and referral when the moisture source is unresolved or remediation is incomplete; the fungi-and-bacteria aggregate does not determine underwriting eligibility.

HO 04 90 (2027-01) separately excludes loss caused by mold, fungus, wet rot, dry rot, bacteria, virus, or other microorganisms even when the condition results from water backup or sump discharge, and addresses odor, staining, contamination, testing, monitoring, assessment, and remediation only as its wording allows.

The 2024-03 HO-3 and 2026-01 DP-3 base forms separately define exclusions for flood, surface water, below-ground water, and sewer, drain, or sump backup, while also distinguishing repeated leakage from sudden or accidental plumbing discharge; Rule 220 source and flood controls therefore support underwriting eligibility but do not decide coverage for a reported loss.

Manual Rule 110 requires reasonable market-value support for the dwelling limit, applies the 80% condition when valuation support is incomplete, and refers higher Coverage A limits for valuation, construction, and exposure review; these valuation controls are separate from roof inspection and age controls.

Florida homeowners appetite rules require a roof inspection before binding at roof age 15 years or greater, prohibit binding at 20 years or greater, and separately apply an actual-cash-value roof schedule at 15 years or greater.

Florida homeowners appetite rules require referral for a requested water-backup limit above $10,000, require a clear water-source description, and distinguish sewer or sump backup from flood, storm surge, and tidal water.

Texas homeowners appetite rules confirm roof inspection before binding at 15 years, no binding at or above 25 years, and a wind-mitigation inspection when Coverage A exceeds $500,000; the Texas product trigger is stricter than the general Manual Rule 200.F threshold above $750,000.

Texas Bulletin B-2021-08 requires separate windstorm and hail deductibles to be stated and consistently disclosed before binding and at renewal, limits named-storm deductibles to at least 1%, hurricane deductibles to no more than 5%, and seacoast wind deductibles to no more than 10%, and prohibits applying a deductible outside the issued policy and supported loss facts.

The 2026-01 DP-3 states that the roof age at which its actual-cash-value roof schedule applies does not determine whether a peril is covered; coverage remains governed by cause of direct physical loss and the policy provisions.
